question: Do learned attention weights in NLP models provide faithful, meaningful explanations of the model's predictions?
hypothesis: If attention were a faithful explanation, it would correlate with gradient/leave-one-out importance and alternative attention weights would change the prediction.
contributions: Correlation of attention with gradient and leave-one-out feature importance across tasks and encoders
Counterfactual attention: random permutation and an adversarial-attention optimisation that finds very different weights giving the same output

method.summary: Train BiLSTM, CNN and average-embedding encoders with additive or scaled dot-product attention on classification, QA and NLI datasets. On test sets, compute Kendall tau between attention and gradient/LOO importance, permute attention 100 times, and optimise adversarial attention distributions within a TVD epsilon of the original output.
method.task: text classification, question answering, natural language inference (analysis of attention explanations)

datasets.name: AG News (Business vs World)
datasets.preprocessing: top 4 categories then world vs business

datasets.name: SNLI
datasets.preprocessing: attention over premise conditioned on hypothesis

models.name: BiLSTM + attention
models.architecture: BiLSTM encoder, additive or scaled dot-product attention, dense decoder
models.init_from: pretrained embeddings (FastText on Simple English Wikipedia for SST, IMDB, 20News, CNN; GloVe 840B for AG News, SNLI; Gensim-trained for MIMIC)
models.tokenizer: spaCy; OOV to <unk>, numeric words to qqq

models.name: Average + attention
models.architecture: linear projection 256 + ReLU per token, no ordering

training.objective: maximum likelihood loss; sigmoid for binary, softmax otherwise

inference.samples: 100 random permutations per instance, median taken; k adversarial distributions per instance (k not stated)

metrics.name: Kendall tau, attention vs gradient (tau_g)
metrics.definition: rank correlation of attention with absolute input gradient per token, gradient not flowing through attention

metrics.name: Kendall tau, attention vs leave-one-out (tau_loo)
metrics.definition: rank correlation of attention with TVD change in output when a token is removed

metrics.name: Median output change under permutation
metrics.definition: median over 100 permutations of TVD(y_perm, y)

metrics.name: epsilon-max JSD
metrics.definition: max JS divergence between original and adversarial attention with TVD of outputs <= epsilon; upper bound 0.69

baselines: Average (feed-forward projection) encoder vs BiLSTM; CNN encoder in supplement
eval.protocol: Test sets only; per-instance statistics shown as histograms by predicted class; Sig. Frac. is fraction of instances where tau is statistically significant (test not named); single trained model per configuration, no seeds stated.

evidence.quote: In practice we simply set this to 0.01 for text classiﬁcation and 0.05 for QA datasets.

limits: Kendall tau over all tokens may be depressed by irrelevant features; agreement on top-k features is untested
Gradients and LOO are not ground truth
Adversarial attention shows existence of alternative heatmaps, not that the model would produce them; they may be unlikely under the attention module's parameters
Multiple plausible explanations may exist; the authors say a 'sufficient' explanation may be reasonable
Only a few attention variants (additive, scaled dot-product) with BiLSTM, CNN, average encoders; no transformers or seq2seq
No seeds, learning rate, batch size or epochs stated

terms.definition: whether attention weights indicate why a model made the prediction that it did
